A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExGRPO study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations and reasoning-trajectory analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds continuous-reward training results, further ablations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds a localized continuous-reward adaptation: batch-normalized, discretized reward standard deviation replaces rollout correctness for difficulty bucketing. The original binary-reward replay pipeline, mixed-policy objective, policy shaping and appendix algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 extends beyond mathematics training and verifiable reasoning evaluation to conversational and instruction-following tasks. It trains on WildChat-IF and evaluates ArenaHardV2, IFEval and IFBench, while retaining the original training data and nine reasoning benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. New Table 2 labels its comparator GRPO, whereas v1 explicitly identifies its on-policy baseline as Dr.GRPO. v2 does not explain whether this denotes a distinct implementation or shorthand for the existing baseline, preventing a reliable comparator-change judgment.

E3.justification: v2 adds a continuous-preference-reward training regime using Qwen2.5-7B-Base, Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B-v0.2 and 7k samples over two epochs. Additional protocols vary Gaussian sampling parameters, reintroduce 10% retired examples every 25 steps, and measure memory and step time. Settings for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Targeted additions test Gaussian sampler width and difficulty bias, whether revisiting mastered queries helps, and replay's memory/runtime costs (Section 6.2 and Appendices E.4–E.5). Existing component ablations, replay-ratio analyses, training dynamics and appendix case studies are preserved.

E5.justification: Both versions report Avg@32 over 32 independent runs for AIME/AMC in the retained evaluation. v2 adds no training-seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests. Reward standard deviation in the new method is a difficulty signal, not additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation scores are retained. Substantial new outcomes include continuous-reward results (Table 2: GRPO 20.0 versus ExGRPO 21.7 average), sampler and retired-query results (Tables 3 and 7), and resource measurements (Table 8). These are additional experiments, not improvements from rerunning the original settings.

T1.justification: Section 5.3 introduces a mathematical definition mapping reward dispersion through batchwise min-max normalization and rounding into discrete difficulty buckets. The original assumptions, Theorem 1, Proposition 2 and their proofs in Appendix D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: correctness/entropy indicators, principled experience management, mixed-policy optimization, and average gains of 3.5/7.6 points across five backbones. The shortened conclusion preserves the performance and stability claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets moderate reward dispersion as useful learning difficulty, retired-query replay as displacing informative examples, and measured overhead as acceptable. Existing interpretations and limitations largely remain; Appendix A still describes evaluation as restricted to verifiable tasks despite the new extension.

D1.justification: Appendix E.5 adds concrete buffer capacity, RAM usage and step timings, including 202,011 trajectories occupying approximately 1.77 GB for the 7B setup. Section 5.3 documents the new training resources and budget. Existing hyperparameters, pseudocode, prompts and code/model links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and positioning around entropy and difficulty-aware methods, distinguishing its bucketing from GRPO-LEAD's advantage reweighting and retirement from Xiong et al.'s prompt filtering. It also cites the new RLHF resources and removes several survey citations, while retaining its central experience-replay positioning.

P1.justification: Changes include localized prose compression, new training-dynamics and ablation subsection headings, sections accommodating the added studies, and relocation of future work to Appendix A. Author information, publication headers, acknowledgments and reference formatting are updated; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 inserts Tables 2, 3, 7 and 8 and reflows retained displays. Figure 1 corrects the panel-caption mapping, replaces High/Low labels with Easy/Hard, and adjusts ticks. Existing visual designs are largely preserved, although some winner bolding in new Tables 3 and 7 contradicts their numerical entries.

improvement.justification: The added sampler and retired-query tests strengthen support for previously untested design choices. Resource measurements clarify the efficiency tradeoff, including 19.0% higher average step time for the 7B model, and the RLHF study provides preliminary evidence beyond verifiable reasoning. These are useful, bounded gains; unchanged uncertainty reporting, misleading winner highlighting and unreconciled limitations reduce the revision's polish and evidential strength.
